newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Treasury restructures, makes new appointments.
newsitem.headline: NZ Treasury restructures, makes new appointments.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Murray Horn on Tuesday announced a series of structural and senior management changes at the Treasury, including the appointment of Iain Rennie as deputy secretary.
Rennie also would be the manager of Treasury's corporate services branch, Horn said.
Rennie replaces John Whitehead, who now heads the regulatory and tax policy branch at Treasury.
Horn also announced that Graeme Wheeler, head of the Debt Management Office (DMO), was leaving Treasury to work at the World Bank in Washington.
The DMO is to merge with the Treasury's commercial and financial branch to create a new branch with operational responsibility for both sides of the crown balance sheet.

The DMO will retain its identity within the new branch and will continue to report to the Treasurer. Geoff Dangerfield, currently branch manager of the commercial and financial branch, will head the new combined branch.
Responsibility for financial reporting will shift from the commercial and financial branch to the budget management branch, which will be responsible for all fiscal and financial reporting.
Responsibility for strategy development and overall policy coordination will shift from the budget management branch to corporate services.
